title: Traffic calming policy approved without speed cushions
subtitle: Also: taxi rates rise, Elliott board appointments, parking licence refusal, Canadian Chinese Heritage Month support.
overview: Council approved the 2026 Traffic Calming Policy Update after a long debate over speed cushions. Councillors voted to remove speed cushions from the policy {{vote:m11}}, over staff advice that they are among the most effective tools for slowing drivers. Council then approved the amended policy {{vote:m14}}.

Council also added direction to track about 200 streets that did not make the list of 25 priority locations, and to review them for other safety measures and report publicly each year. It allowed temporary speed cushions for construction detours {{vote:m15}}. Council directed staff to remove existing speed cushions from bike lanes, subject to $60,000 in the 2027 budget {{vote:m16}}.

Other business included a 6.7 per cent taxi rate increase, passed on the consent report. Council appointed three members to The Elliott Community Board of Trustees {{vote:m2}}, refused a private parking agent licence {{vote:m17}}, and backed a call for a federal Canadian Chinese Heritage Month {{vote:m18}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2026 Traffic Calming Policy Update as amended {{vote:m14}}.
Council removed the use of speed cushions from the Traffic Calming Policy {{vote:m11}}.
Staff must keep an internal registry of about 200 streets outside the 25 prioritized locations, review them for other Vision Zero measures, and report publicly each year {{vote:m13}}.
Temporary speed cushions may be used to manage traffic on construction detours {{vote:m15}}.
Staff will remove existing speed cushions from bike lanes if $60,000 is added in the 2027 budget, and report on alternative protection methods before then {{vote:m16}}.
Staff will amend the Taxicab by-law to raise taxicab rates by 6.7 per cent, effective April 1, 2026 or at the City's meter check.
Kimberley Wilson was appointed, and Justine Garner and Naeem Mir re-appointed, to The Elliott Community Board of Trustees for terms ending April 2029 {{vote:m2}}.
Council supports a federal call for an annual Canadian Chinese Heritage Month and will send the resolution to the Prime Minister, a federal minister and two MPs {{vote:m18}}.

debate: Delegates and the mover of the amendment said speed cushions can cause pain or injury for some people with disabilities. Delegates also said avoiding them is costly and impractical when relying on ride-hailing or taxis, and asked for other measures such as road narrowing and curb extensions.

Staff opposed removing speed cushions. They said it is one of 22 tools, not a first choice, and that some narrow, long streets have few alternatives. They said it reduces speeds more than other measures, now that automated speed enforcement is no longer available.

Councillors who opposed removal worried about road safety and noted that the newer cushion design lets drivers straddle it and leaves a gap for emergency vehicles. One councillor said that, given the other 21 tools, removal still leaves many options.
Councillors raised a possible human rights complaint risk. Staff said legal counsel was not available on the file, so it could not be explored in closed session.

After the vote, staff said construction-detour cushions might also be barred. This led to the separate motion permitting temporary cushions, with staff aiming to keep at least one route free of vertical measures.

On bike lanes, supporters said the cushions block accessible cycles and are a risk to children. One councillor opposed the cost and the lack of a defined alternative. Staff said each site would need its own design.
